source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Houston publishes 84 MW of IT capacity across two buildings totaling 347,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 84 MW of IT load is roughly 2,100 racks. This campus ranks first among the 18 Texas facilities with published capacity figures and accounts for 18% of the 468 MW of total published data center IT capacity in the state.

HOU3 holds a 3-Globe Green Globes certification and HOU4 holds a 2-Globe certification, qualifying both for energy-efficient operations. The certifications do not specify whether the campus can host GPU-intensive workloads or the power density it is designed to deliver to individual racks. Without rack-level power specifications, the site's actual utility for large-scale AI compute deployment remains unclear.

CyrusOne divested its Houston assets in March 2022 for 670 million dollars, but the acquiring party name was not confirmed in available sources this session. CyrusOne's own operator page as of September 2026 still brands and lists full specifications for HOU3-HOU4 under the CyrusOne name, consistent with continued CyrusOne branding or operation, though this does not resolve the ownership status after the 2022 transaction. Ownership verification remains flagged for a future research pass.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
